mini_abstract: A 24-participant study of how head-following AR windows and their delay affect perceived resistance and task load.
abstract: Head-following virtual windows keep content within view in augmented reality, but their motion can induce a sense of resistance during head movement. In a 24-participant study, we investigated window-following behavior, delay, and window size, and measured perceived resistance and subjective task load.
contributions: Evaluated perceived resistance and task load for Head-Locked and Tag-Along AR windows.
Examined how window-following delay and window size influence the user experience.
results: Tag-Along windows and longer delays increased perceived resistance and task load in the study.
Window size alone did not significantly affect perceived resistance; its effects depended on interface behavior.
presentation: Oral presentation by Motoki Kagami at IEEE VR 2026.
my_role: Carried out the implementation, study design, data collection, analysis, and manuscript writing in collaboration with the coauthors.

mini_abstract: A 46-sensor tactile glove for recognizing 10 Japanese fingerspelling signs, evaluated with five participants.
abstract: We present a tactile sensing glove with 46 force-sensitive Velostat sensors for Japanese Sign Language (JSL) vocabulary recognition. Using LSTM and k-NN with Dynamic Time Warping on 10 JSL finger-spelling signs collected from 5 participants, we achieve test accuracies of 76% and 87% respectively, demonstrating the potential of sensor-based SLR without reliance on vision-based approaches.
contributions: Developed a low-cost, portable tactile glove with 46 Velostat pressure sensors strategically placed at finger joints and fingertips
Designed a preprocessing pipeline with baseline correction, moving average filtering, and Min-Max normalization for cross-subject generalization
Compared LSTM and k-NN with DTW on a 10-class JSL finger-spelling dataset using group 5-fold cross-validation
results: k-NN with Dynamic Time Warping achieved 87% average accuracy (Precision 0.88, Recall 0.87, F1 0.85)
LSTM achieved 76% test accuracy; dropout and L2 regularization were applied to reduce overfitting on the limited dataset
presentation: Oral presentation by Motoki Kagami at MCSoC 2024.
my_role: Carried out device assembly, data collection, model implementation, analysis, and manuscript writing. PCB design and fabrication were performed by collaborators.
